## TL;DR

Ran a headless end-to-end pass of the update and restart notice against an auth-less server from a detached scratch worktree. The UI matrix covered hand-run, systemd, launchd, RepoOS-managed, and uncertain supervisor states at desktop and phone widths. It exposed two presentation bugs: the release notice was unstyled and inaccessible below the phone navigation, and the restart failure copy was squeezed into a narrow side column on phones. Both are fixed and have a regression assertion. The required changed-path check passed after formatting.

## Work and rationale

I started by reading the task specification and tracing the existing flow through `ReleaseUpdateNotification.vue`, `/api/update-status`, and the restart path tests. The repository already had unit coverage for supervisor classifications, uncertain detection, accepted and failed restart responses, and waiting-for-idle behavior. The earlier releases QA report covered supervisor variants visually, but this task calls for exercising the combined update/restart flow against a running app. I kept those existing test boundaries intact and focused this pass on browser behavior, interaction, and visual failures.

To satisfy the browser constraint, I created a detached scratch worktree under this task worktree's ignored `.repoos` directory. I ran `just serve-noauth 7296` there and confirmed its live `/api/health` and `/api/update-status` responses identify the scratch root and the running version. Playwright ran headlessly against that server. Its page routes replaced the update/restart responses with fixture payloads; the app shell and all other requests still came from the live server. The request stub never called a service manager, signalled a process, or restarted the server.

I exercised both the available-release dialog and the installed-version restart dialog. The matrix included hand-run, external systemd, external launchd, a RepoOS-managed service, and uncertain supervisor detection, each at 1440px and 390px. For the actionable states, the browser clicked Restart when idle, checked the waiting state, cancelled it, and checked that the normal actions returned. It then clicked Restart now: systemd, launchd, and managed fixtures returned an accepted restart; the hand-run fixture also exercised a simulated 503 with a manager failure. The uncertain fixture showed a root-and-port-scoped manual command and no automatic restart action. All ten platform/viewport cases passed after the two UI fixes.

The first phone-width run showed that the available-release notice had no component styles. It flowed after the app shell, where the fixed bottom tab bar intercepted its click. I added a compact floating card style, placed it above the phone navigation using the existing safe-area token, and marked it as a body-level overlay layer so it remains a valid hit target under Radix dialogs. A Playwright click then opened the release details at 390px. The notice keeps the existing copy, keyboard activation, and dismissal behavior.

Reviewing the failure screenshot showed that the restart error paragraph shared a flex row with the hand-run explanation. That left both blocks in narrow columns on a phone. I let the action row wrap and gave the hand-run block and alert a full row. The error guidance now reads as a single block below the controls, while the retry buttons remain available. The release UI test asserts the floating/mobile positioning and full-width error rule; the focused releases test file passed all 45 tests.

## Approaches tried

I first tried to click the available-release banner while the installed-version modal was open. Playwright correctly reported that the modal overlay intercepted the pointer. That was a sequence problem in the harness, not a product bug: the real UI intentionally gives modal focus to the restart notice. I updated the sequence to close the restart notice, inspect the separate update dialog, then clear only the test page's remembered dismissal and reload before exercising restart actions.

The first mobile screenshot also showed the underlying issue clearly: the banner content appeared below the phone tab bar and could not receive a tap. I treated that as a product defect because it reproduced in the real app shell, then verified the fixed component in the same browser sequence. The mobile failure screenshot exposed another issue beyond the text assertions, so I added a bounding-box assertion to make sure the alert spans most of the dialog width. Captures for the run were kept under ignored `.repoos/qa-restart-1196/`; no image files were added to the branch.

## Challenges and blockers

Supervisor and restart outcomes in this pass were fixtures, not live systemd or launchd installations. The only actual server I operated was the hand-run auth-less dev server used to serve the UI and check its health/status endpoints. That server was shut down cleanly after the browser run. I do not claim that real supervisor commands, service permissions, process handover, or reconnect timing were exercised. The existing automated server tests remain the evidence for those internal routing decisions, and the task's QA note records this limit explicitly.

The first required RepoOS check failed at format check because the new test assertion had not yet been formatted. Per repository instructions, I ran `bun run fmt` and repeated the exact changed-path check. The second pass passed. Its remote phase built the project and passed 174 scoped tests plus the two timing tests run in isolation; local checks then passed format, lint, build, CSS layering, theme and rendered contrast, bare-require, branch-artifact, and UI smoke checks. No config or task metadata was edited, and no source was changed after that passing check.

## Key learnings

An interaction can pass a component test while still being unreachable in the complete app shell. The update banner's click handler worked, but its missing positioning and the phone navigation's hit area made it unusable at a narrow viewport. The live shell plus headless click uncovered this gap. A screenshot of the full error state also provided evidence that checking text alone would have missed the narrow-column failure layout.

For follow-up QA, testing supervisor combinations through injected API fixtures is useful for deterministic UI coverage, but it should be reported separately from real service operations. Here the matrix verifies what each supervisor state presents and how the controls respond to accepted, waiting, cancellation, and failure responses. It does not prove the operating system's service manager can restart a real installation. The QA document keeps that boundary clear so a future live-device or service-owner pass can supply the remaining evidence.
